heading: INT. ST. AGNES LYING-IN HOSPITAL - CONSULTING ROOM - DAY

units.text: INT. ST. AGNES LYING-IN HOSPITAL - CONSULTING ROOM - DAY
London, 1923.
Rain falls on the high windows without stopping.
The gas lamp on the wall makes a small yellow light.
The room smells of carbolic soap and old wood.
Margaret sits on a hard chair.
Her husband Edmund stands near the window and does not look at her.
The doctor sits behind a big desk with many papers.
Mrs. Ashworth, you have been married six years. There is no child. This is the third time you come to me.
units.name: DR. WHITCOMBE
paren: he opens a file and reads slowly

units.text: Yes, doctor. We hope you have some new idea.
units.name: MARGARET
paren: her hands are tight in her lap

units.text: The rain becomes stronger.
A cart passes in the street below and its wheels make a loud noise on the stones.
In the corridor a clock strikes the half hour.
It is not an idea we need. It is an answer. My family asks me every Sunday. Every Sunday.
units.name: EDMUND
paren: he turns from the window, his voice is cold

units.text: Mr. Ashworth, I must say it plainly. The examination shows no fault in your wife.
units.name: DR. WHITCOMBE
paren: he closes the file

units.text: A long quiet.
The lamp makes a small sound.
Outside, a bell rings far away, and the grey light on the wall becomes darker.
Then the fault is not mine.
units.name: MARGARET
paren: she looks up at him for the first time

units.text: You say this to me? In front of her?
units.name: EDMUND
paren: he steps forward, his hand on the desk

units.text: I say what is true. Please sit down.
units.name: DR. WHITCOMBE
paren: he stands, calm but not soft

units.text: Edmund does not sit.
He walks to the door, he stops, he comes back.
His face is red, and the rain is loud now, and the room feels very small.
The door opens without a knock.
SISTER BRIGID, a tall nurse in a starched white veil, comes in with a metal tray.
She puts it down and she stands very straight beside the desk.
Doctor, forgive me. The results you asked for from the laboratory. Both sets.
units.name: SISTER BRIGID
paren: her voice is quiet but it carries

units.text: Thank you, Sister. Stay, please.
units.name: DR. WHITCOMBE
paren: he takes the paper and reads it, and his face changes

units.text: Give me that.
units.name: EDMUND
paren: he reaches for the paper

units.text: Sir, it is not yours to take.
units.name: SISTER BRIGID
paren: she puts her hand flat on the tray

units.text: Edmund. Please. Sit.
units.name: MARGARET
paren: very softly

units.text: Do not tell me what to do! Six years I wait. Six years my mother looks at you like you are a broken clock!
units.name: EDMUND
paren: he turns on her, loud

units.text: Thunder, low and long, across the roofs of the city.
The lamp shakes.
The window glass hums.
The laboratory is certain, Mr. Ashworth. The difficulty is with you. Not with her. It was never with her.
units.name: DR. WHITCOMBE
paren: he holds up the paper

units.text: That is a lie. That is a doctor's lie to make a woman feel better.
units.name: EDMUND
paren: he stops, he cannot speak, then he laughs one time

units.text: You never once asked if it was you. Not once. You looked at me. Always at me.
units.name: MARGARET
paren: she stands, her chair scrapes the floor

units.text: Enough!
units.name: EDMUND
paren: he knocks the tray from the desk, the instruments fall and ring on the floor

units.text: You will leave this room now, sir. Or I will call the porters.
units.name: SISTER BRIGID
paren: she does not move back, her chin lifts

units.text: The rain falls on.
A long moment.
Edmund looks at the three of them, at the paper, at the wet window, and he takes his hat from the chair and he goes out.
The door shakes in its frame.
He will not come home tonight.
units.name: MARGARET
paren: she sits down slowly, and begins to breathe again

units.text: Then you will stay here, Mrs. Ashworth. Sister Brigid will make you tea.
units.name: DR. WHITCOMBE
paren: gently

units.text: Strong tea. With sugar.
units.name: SISTER BRIGID
paren: she bends and picks up the instruments one by one

units.text: The clock in the corridor strikes the hour.
The rain is soft again.
The lamp is steady.
